title: Law of Agency: Duties, Disclosure & Conflict
originality: All items original to LicensePath. Modeled on the DRE exam blueprint and style only; no actual exam items reproduced.

questions.stem: A principal is the person who:
rationales: Correct. A principal authorizes agency action.

questions.stem: A seller tells a listing agent their lowest acceptable price. The agent should:
options: Protect it as confidential unless authorized
rationales: Correct. A client bottom line is normally confidential without authorization.
Correct. Actual authority is intentionally conferred.
A friend cannot necessarily confer it.

questions.stem: An agent promises a seller will provide a roof credit without seller approval. The key problem is lack of:
rationales: Correct. The agent should not speak for a principal without authority.
A card does not grant authority.
Correct. Core duties include loyalty and confidentiality.
Obedience extends only to lawful instructions.

questions.stem: A client directs agent to hide a known material defect. The agent should:
rationales: Loyalty does not authorize dishonest conduct.
Correct. Material disclosure issues require lawful handling and broker involvement.
Buyer type does not remove duties.
Deleting photos does not erase knowledge.

options: Same broker representing buyer and seller
rationales: Correct. Dual agency means one broker represents both sides in a transaction.

questions.stem: In dual agency, an agent should not reveal:
options: A client's confidential bottom line without authorization
rationales: Correct. Confidential bargaining information remains protected.

options: Later approves an unauthorized act with material knowledge
rationales: Correct. Ratification is later approval with knowledge.

questions.stem: A broker's conduct makes a third party reasonably believe an agent has authority. This describes:
rationales: Correct. Apparent authority arises from reasonable appearance based on principal conduct.
Correct. Disclosure should support informed choice.
Required disclosure is not merely optional.

questions.stem: A conflict of interest should be handled by:
options: Early identification, disclosure, and broker process
rationales: Correct. Conflicts require transparent authorized management.

questions.stem: An agent wants to buy their client's listing through a friend. The agent should first:
options: Notify broker and use required conflict disclosure
Tell seller it is best offer
rationales: Correct. Personal interest requires early broker review and disclosure.
Price opinion does not cure conflict.

questions.stem: A material client instruction should be preserved in:
rationales: Correct. Material instructions require durable records.
Social posts are not secure files.
Correct. Closing does not automatically erase confidentiality.
Texts are not the relevant event.
A showing is not necessarily relationship end.

questions.stem: When representation is uncertain, the best agent action is to:
options: Clarify relationship, use approved disclosures, and consult broker
rationales: Correct. Clarification and supervision protect all parties.
